results.evidence: The Mountain Project page lists 2 pitches but gives 7000 ft (2121 m), which is plainly a peak-level elevation figure, not a route length; length_m 2134 is that same number in metres. The row's gear text says only 2 pitches. No source states the true length. Searched MP, general web, guidebook index PDFs; no second independent page found.

Mountain Project lists the chimney at 7000 ft (2121 m), the same peak-level figure copied onto neighbouring routes; no pitch count is shown there. The row's hazards, overview (Pitch 1, Pitch 2) and gear (both pitches) all describe two short pitches, so 2134 m is impossible. No source states the true length.

results.correct_value: five rope-length pitches (35-65 m) then ridge
results.evidence: The Mountain Project description numbers (1) 55 m, (2) 60 m, (3) 65 m, (4) 52 m, (5) 35 m, then (6) the roughly 300 m Underhill Ridge to the summit; its header says 6 pitches counting the ridge. So there are five 35-65 m pitches, not six 55-65 m. The row's overview agrees. Only one independent page found (searched AAJ, SummitPost, openbeta mirror of the same text).

The only page found (Mountain Project) lists 350 ft, 3 pitches in its header while its text says three chossy pitches reach the ridge plus two more along the ridge (5 total). Another MP entry for the same route has no description or pitch count. Searched MP, area pages, general web for a second source; none exists. Header 3 is arguably the face pitches only.

The overview numbers P1-P4 and the descent text refers to the top of the fourth pitch, with a further chossy pitch to the summit ledge; Mountain Project's Symmetry Spire list shows 5 pitches while the route page shows none. So 1 is certainly wrong but 4 versus 5 is not settled, so it is blanked.

Both the Mountain Project page and the AAJ write-up give 660 ft (about 201 m) and 9 pitches, agreeing with length_m. The per-pitch metre figures in the overview (summing about 295 m) come from the same guidebook text and no source gives corrected pitch lengths, so no prose number can be fixed from two sources.

Mountain Project header says 5 pitches while its text lists p1-p6 (p2 only 7 m, followed by the trail) and says 3 more pitches above the trail after the 2 below, which gives 5; the sixth entry is unexplained. Searched MP area pages, SuperTopo, trip reports; no second source with a pitch breakdown.
